concept_html:
A virtual environment is a folder with its own Python interpreter link and its own site-packages. Packages you install there do not touch the system Python or any other project.

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e . --group dev

Rules that prevent most "it worked yesterday" problems:

  • One environment per project. Two projects that share an environment share their version conflicts. Upgrading pandas for one breaks the other.
  • Never install into the system Python. Operating systems and other tools depend on it.
  • Use python -m pip, not bare pip. Bare pip runs whichever pip comes first on your PATH, which may belong to a different interpreter. python -m pip always installs into the interpreter you are about to run.
  • Keep .venv/ out of Git. It is large, machine-specific and rebuildable. Commit pyproject.toml and a lock file instead (lesson B6-L3).

In code, sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix is True inside a virtual environment. A script that must not run against the system Python can check it and stop.

Sometimes one project needs two environments, because two dependencies cannot live together. A real case from this course's own build: PySpark 4.0.4 fails to import its pandas integration with pandas 3.x, so the Spark test harness runs in its own environment pinned to pandas 2.x, while the rest uses pandas 3. Separate environments, each fully pinned, beat one environment held together by guesswork.

Tools such as uv create and sync environments much faster, and conda manages non-Python libraries. The principles are the same.

exercises.prompt: Write `require_virtualenv()`. It raises `RuntimeError` with the message `"activate the project's virtual environment first"` when the running interpreter is not inside a virtual environment, and returns `None` otherwise. Read `sys.prefix` and `sys.base_prefix` when the function is called, not at import time.
exercises.prompt_html: Write require_virtualenv(). It raises RuntimeError with the message "activate the project's virtual environment first" when the running interpreter is not inside a virtual environment, and returns None otherwise. Read sys.prefix and sys.base_prefix when the function is called, not at import time.
exercises.solution:
import sys


def require_virtualenv() -> None:
    """Stop when not running inside a virtual environment.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If sys.prefix equals sys.base_prefix.
    """
    if sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix:
        raise RuntimeError("activate the project's virtual environment first")

title: One virtual environment per project, and python -m pip
why_html:
An analyst runs pip install statsmodels in a terminal, then python analysis.py in the same terminal, and gets ModuleNotFoundError. pip belonged to one Python, and python to another. They try sudo pip install, which upgrades NumPy in the system Python and breaks a command-line tool the operating system uses. Two hours are gone.

python -m venv .venv, activation, and python -m pip install make the interpreter that installs and the interpreter that runs the same one.
